summary:
COSMIC CHAOS is an interactive 2D space adventure developed by Team BananaNasa using Unity. The game transforms space science and mission engineering into an engaging, hands-on learning experience where players become astronauts, prepare their spacecraft, assemble rockets, and explore the solar system.

Players begin by equipping spacecraft interiors and assembling seven rocket components before launching into space. An interactive solar system allows them to explore Mercury, Venus, Mars, and Jupiter, each offering unique puzzles, NPC interactions, and gameplay challenges. Players manage scientific instruments, mass, power, and budget on Mercury, test their memory through Venus’s Cloud Memory challenge, explore Mars, and experiment with gravity-assisted navigation in Jupiter’s Moon Slingshot. Completing planetary puzzles unlocks new destinations and rewards players with discovery certificates.

Inspired by NASA’s SLS and Orion, MESSENGER mission data, and ESA and JAXA’s BepiColombo mission, COSMIC CHAOS brings real space science into simplified educational simulations.

Our project addresses the challenge by combining spacecraft design, engineering trade-offs, resource management, and scientific exploration with entertaining gameplay. It encourages students to develop problem-solving skills, curiosity, and an understanding of space mission design. By making complex space concepts accessible and enjoyable, COSMIC CHAOS empowers players to learn by doing and explore by playing.
details:
COSMIC CHAOS: Build. Launch. Explore.

Project Overview

COSMIC CHAOS is an interactive 2D space adventure game developed by Team BananaNasa to transform complex space science and mission engineering concepts into an engaging, hands-on learning experience. The game allows players to become astronauts, prepare their spacecraft, assemble rockets, explore different planets, solve scientific challenges, and earn discovery rewards.

Our project addresses the Space Mission Design Game challenge by combining spacecraft preparation, engineering decisions, resource management, scientific exploration, and interactive gameplay into a single educational adventure.

How the Game Works

The player begins by preparing the spacecraft interior, placing essential equipment in designated areas such as the living area and exercise/storage area. Visual guides, drag-and-drop mechanics, and instant feedback help players understand how spacecraft interiors are organized to support life in space.

Next, players enter the Rocket Assembly Bay, where they assemble seven rocket components inspired by NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) and Orion spacecraft. Players must identify and match each component to its correct position. Once all seven components are successfully installed, the rocket can launch, accompanied by animated flames and smoke effects.

After liftoff, players access an interactive Solar System Navigation interface, where they can select Mercury, Venus, Mars, or Jupiter. Each planet introduces unique challenges, NPC interactions, puzzles, and gameplay mechanics.

  • Mercury – Mission to Mercury: Players select scientific instruments and manage engineering constraints such as spacecraft mass, power consumption, and budget. The mission introduces polar ice research and demonstrates how engineering decisions influence scientific objectives.
  • Venus – Cloud Memory: Players complete a timed memory challenge by matching eight pairs of cards, encouraging observation, concentration, and quick decision-making.
  • Mars – Planetary Exploration: Players encounter planet-specific puzzles and gameplay challenges as part of their solar system exploration journey.
  • Jupiter – Moon Slingshot: Players experiment with launch angles and propulsion power to navigate Jupiter's gravitational environment and reach three moons. This simplified simulation introduces gravity-assisted navigation and trajectory planning.

Throughout the adventure, players can meet NPCs, solve planetary strip puzzles, reveal new destinations, and receive a Certificate of Planet Discovery. These rewards encourage continued exploration and provide a sense of achievement.

Scientific and Educational Foundation

COSMIC CHAOS draws inspiration from publicly available information provided by NASA and other space agencies:

  • NASA Space Launch System (SLS) and Orion: Hardware references inspire the rocket assembly components and launch experience.
  • NASA MESSENGER and Planetary Data System (PDS): Mercury exploration findings, including evidence of polar water ice, inspire scientific objectives and instrument selection.
  • ESA and JAXA BepiColombo: Planetary flybys and scientific instruments inspire mission planning and gravity-assisted navigation.

The project adapts real scientific principles into simplified educational simulations, making them accessible to players without advanced knowledge of aerospace engineering.

Tools and Technologies

We developed COSMIC CHAOS using Unity as our primary game engine and C# as our programming language. The game incorporates:

  • Unity 2D for scene development, rendering, animations, and gameplay.
  • C# for game logic, drag-and-drop interactions, puzzle systems, resource management, scoring, and scene transitions.
  • Digital 2D artwork, spacecraft assets, and planetary textures for visual environments.
  • Unity UI components for interactive menus, mission interfaces, progress indicators, and player feedback.

The game is designed to run on a standard computer using a keyboard and mouse. No specialized hardware, sensors, or external equipment is required.

Creativity and Innovation

COSMIC CHAOS stands out by combining multiple gameplay genres within a unified space exploration experience. Rather than relying solely on traditional educational explanations, our game allows players to learn through experimentation, visual interaction, problem-solving, and exploration.

Each planet offers a different gameplay experience, reflecting distinct scientific concepts and environmental characteristics. The combination of realistic spacecraft imagery, interactive rocket assembly, planetary navigation, NPC-guided activities, memory puzzles, gravity-based challenges, and discovery certificates makes learning both immersive and rewarding.

The game also connects scientific knowledge with practical decision-making. For example, Mercury's instrument selection requires players to consider engineering trade-offs, while Jupiter's Moon Slingshot encourages experimentation with trajectory and propulsion.

Design Considerations

Our team considered several factors during development:

  • Educational accuracy: Using NASA and partner-agency scientific information as the foundation while simplifying complex concepts for gameplay.
  • Accessibility: Designing intuitive controls, clear instructions, visual guides, and immediate feedback for players with different levels of scientific
